matches.rationale: Finding pred_id 1 claims the abstract says '6.8×' and '5.1–7.2×', while the ground truth corruption has the abstract stating 'up to 4.2×' and '3.2–4.5×'. The numbers and the basis of inconsistency (abstract vs. introduction in the finding, vs. experimental figures in the ground truth) differ, so they refer to different corruptions.
Finding pred_id 4 directly identifies the same logical inconsistency: the text defines burst tolerance as a difference while Equation (1) defines it as a ratio.
No finding addresses the omission of baseline configuration details (batch sizes, KV cache settings, etc.) in Section 4.1.
No finding targets the specific text accompanying Figure 6 that inflates throughput gains to 'up to 4.5× and 3.2×' when the actual ratios are lower.
No finding mentions the unsupported generalization that results apply to 'all MLLM architectures' (cross-attention, prefix-tuning, adapters) when only two architectures were tested.
Finding pred_id 3 precisely identifies the fabricated citation '[61]' and the claim about Zhang et al. proposing similar work in 2024, matching the ground truth.
No finding discusses the undefined penalty factor β in Equation (3) or the inconsistent switch from decode to prefill context.
No finding raises the ethical omission regarding user consent, terms-of-service compliance, or IRB review for the web-scraped datasets.
No finding detects the promotional, absolute claim in the Introduction that ElasticMM 'completely eliminates all inference bottlenecks.'
No finding points out the narrative inconsistency that the abstract lists unified multimodal prefix caching as a scheduling technique while it is introduced later in a separate section.
No finding addresses the ablation study text that claims both optimizations provide 'roughly equal performance gains' despite one likely contributing more.
No finding reports the unfair comparison that ElasticMM was tested with optimized CUDA kernels and custom memory allocators not available to baselines.
No finding challenges the Conclusion's absolute claim that ElasticMM 'guarantees SLO compliance under all workload conditions' despite evidence of limits.
Finding pred_id 2 concerns a misattributed reference number for LLaMA3.2-Vision, not the false claim that Vaswani et al. introduced the encoder-decoder paradigm for multimodal models.
No finding mentions the omission of limitations, potential failure modes, environmental costs, or societal impact discussion in the Conclusion.
